Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - 19-year-old female with several days-to-1-week history of burning pain on urination and increased urinary frequency.
  - Today noticed pink-colored urine; no clear frank red blood reported.
  - No fevers, vomiting, or back/ flank pain.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Symptoms began about a week ago; burning on voiding and polyuria; current episode includes pink urine.
- ENT symptoms:
  - None reported.
- Distribution of symptoms (lips/face/uvula/etc.):
  - Not applicable (urinary symptoms; no facial/neck swelling or ENT involvement).
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior UTI documented in history.
  - History of IBS.
  - On combined oral contraceptive pill.
  - IBS medication starting with “M” (exact name not documented).
  - Allergies: documented allergy to clindamycin.
  - Prior injections/ED/hospitalizations: none mentioned.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: clindamycin (reported).
  - Current medications: combined oral contraceptive pill; IBS med starting with M (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context:
  - Living in university halls with a roommate.
  - Sexual activity: not currently sexually active; last unprotected intercourse about 1–2 weeks ago; last period two weeks ago.
  - Cannabis use: smoked cannabis once about 1.5 weeks ago; advised by clinician to avoid regular use.
- Any other relevant points:
  - General health otherwise: eating/drinking OK; IBS noted; no fevers or systemic symptoms.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution:
  - Not examined; no ENT findings documented.
- Airway/breathing:
  - Not applicable; no airway symptoms reported.
- Mental status:
  - Not described.
- Vitals/examination findings:
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with patient:
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Primary impression:
  - Suspected acute urinary tract infection (cystitis) given burning urination, increased frequency, suprapubic pain, and pink urine; absence of fever/back pain makes more serious infection less likely.
- Key justifications:
  - Onset within the past week; urinary symptoms with discomfort on voiding; pink urine today; no systemic symptoms.
- Additional notes:
  - Allergy to clindamycin documented.
  - Pregnancy risk assessment discussed; patient on combined pill; last period two weeks ago.
  - No ENT-related findings or concerns identified.
  - If uncertainty or conflicting statements exist, none noted.

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  - Urine sample to be collected today for lab analysis (drop-off at practice; results to be communicated).
  - Initiate antibiotic therapy with one of the following for 3 days: Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin (exact agent chosen/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Acetaminophen (dose/route/frequency not documented) for pain as needed.
  - Advise increased fluid intake and hydration.
- Instructions to patient/caregiver:
  - If fever, back pain, vomiting, or symptoms worsen, contact medical care or return.
  - Urine sample collection details provided; results will guide antibiotic choice.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Fever, back pain, vomiting, worsening urinary symptoms despite treatment—return for re-evaluation.
- Follow-up:
  - If symptoms do not improve by next week, return for re-evaluation.
- Additional notes:
  - Counseling provided regarding cannabis use (noting that clinician advised avoiding regular cannabis use).
  - No COVID-19 vaccine-related decisions discussed.
